clue.text: Authority to convert the police into riflemen?

definitions.text: Authority to convert the police into riflemen?

parts.words: Authority to convert the police into riflemen?
parts.note: to rifle is to ransack or search through, so a document that lets officers go through your house and drawers turns them, jokingly, into 'riflemen'

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about what order would turn police constables into soldiers carrying rifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riflemen' looks military, but here it means men who rifle, that is search, a property; the authority for that is a court document.
explanation.definitionFit: A court document authorising police to search premises, the riflers of the cryptic reading.

clue.text: Game wherein money counts reading between the lines

definitions.text: Game wherein money counts reading between the lines

parts.words: Game wherein money counts reading between the lines
parts.note: a pub game where old coins are pushed up a board and score when they come to rest in the beds between lines marked on it

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a game in which cash matters to anyone reading between the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: A British pub game: old coins are struck up a board and score if they settle between parallel lines; 'reading between the lines' usually means inferring.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional pub board game played with old British coins scoring between marked lines.

clue.text: One way to raise a sign

indicators.note: the letters of raise can be ordered in more than one way, and this is one arrangement

explanation.surface: Suggests a method of lifting up a placard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way to' arrange RAISE is the anagram; 'sign' is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram, first of the twelve zodiac signs.

clue.text: Pin-up picture of a little tart

definitions.meaning: slang for a glamour photograph of a scantily clad model
a sweet baked dessert with a crumb base and soft cheese filling

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a glamour photograph; also a dessert of soft cheese on a biscuit base.

clue.text: Battling with iron rations ?

definitions.meaning: emergency food carried by soldiers, read as ..., the food of war

explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict; and, read in two words, the food of soldiers in battle.

clue.text: Drew one out to provide with new finance

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of drew one are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone withdrew a pound to give fresh funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a fresh endowment or funding again.

clue.text: A student thus finishes' as well

indicators.note: the word for thus comes at the end of the assembly

parts.note: L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
thus means so

explanation.surface: A student ends up doing the same thing as well.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner, a student driver in Britain; 'finishes' places SO last.
explanation.definitionFit: Too or in addition: a synonym meaning likewise.

clue.text: But Stonehenge feature weighs over 42lb

definitions.meaning: two upright stones with a lintel across them, as at Stonehenge
42lb is three stone in British weight, and this structure is three stones, weighing far more

explanation.walkthrough: A stone is 14lb in British weights, so 42lb is three stone; the structure is literally three stones, each weighing tons.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalithic structure of two uprights and a lintel; literally three stones, so more than three stone.

clue.text: Treasury to Oliver ? What a lot of flannel !

parts.note: a chest is a box for keeping treasure or funds
Oliver Cromwell ruled England as Lord Protector

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a lot of empty talk about Cromwell and the treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flannel' looks like waffle, but it is the cloth: a pad of flannel worn on the chest against cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned garment of warm flannel cloth worn over the torso against chills.

clue.text: Source of a peace offering

parts.note: a peace offering is figuratively an olive branch, and the branch comes from the plant that grows it

explanation.surface: A question about where a gesture of reconciliation comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'offer an olive branch' means to make peace, so the plant bearing the branch is the source.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive branch symbolises peace, and the plant it is cut from is its origin.

clue.text: Smart from the birch

definitions.meaning: smart in the sense of fashionable or stylish
the whooshing sound of a birch rod swung through the air in a caning

explanation.definitionFit: Stylish slang for elegant; also the hissing sound a birch cane makes when swung.

clue.text: Chain letters

parts.note: not the pyramid-scheme mail but S-shaped links: a collar of S-shaped links is a heraldic chain worn by officials

explanation.surface: A nod to the chain letters that circulate promising luck to those who pass them on.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'collar of esses' is a ceremonial chain made of S-shaped links, worn for example by the Lord Chief Justice; the letters are S's, plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the letter S, and the S-shaped links forming a ceremonial collar chain.

clue.text: Helps to construct dais

indicators.note: building something new out of the letters of dais means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Volunteers lend a hand to put up a platform for speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Assists, as a verb: a helper is said to assist or support.

clue.text: (Cause of) greeting coming through the rye ?

definitions.text: (Cause of) greeting coming through the rye

parts.words: (Cause of) greeting coming through the rye
parts.note: Burns's song 'Comin' Thro' the Rye' asks 'Gin a body ... a body', and in Scots 'greet' means to weep, so the salute makes a lass cry

explanation.surface: A question about what greeting is exchanged by people meeting in a rye field.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Burns song 'Comin' Thro' the Rye', 'Gin a body kiss a body, need a body cry?'; 'greeting' is both a salute and Scots for weeping, hence the bracketed 'Cause of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a form of greeting, and in the Burns song the one exchanged in the rye.

clue.text: Like the case of a leading Roman ladygetting one in the mug?

parts.note: prima is the Italian feminine for first, as in prima donna

indicators.note: one is placed inside the word for the mug

parts.note: mug is slang for face
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Describes a lawsuit about a top Roman woman getting struck in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting one in' puts I inside FACE; 'Like the case' recalls the legal phrase for a case that looks sound on first view.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal Latin meaning at first sight, as in a case that appears sound before deeper scrutiny.

clue.text: Half a thesis contributed to a newspaper

definitions.meaning: the first three letters of thesis spell the definite ... of English grammar
a piece of writing supplied to a paper for publication

explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical part of speech like 'the', and a written piece published in a newspaper.

clue.text: The alternative to 'call-up is speculative

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness is called

explanation.surface: Suggests that the option instead of conscription is only a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CITE to ETIC in this down clue; 'call-up' looks like conscription.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypothetical, concerned with ideas rather than practice.

clue.text: Address to a magistrate in a church service

definitions.meaning: 'Your ...' is the British form of address for a magistrate or mayor
a religious gathering of praise in church

explanation.definitionFit: The honorific in 'Your Worship' used to a British magistrate, and a religious service of devotion.

clue.text: Sunspot envisaged on earth

parts.note: not a dark patch on the sun's surface but a small brown spot brought out on the skin of a face by sunshine

explanation.surface: An astronomer's dark solar blemish, but seen from down here on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Envisaged' hides 'in the face': a sunspot that appears on someone's visage, a skin mark caused by sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown pigmented skin mark brought out by exposure to sunlight.

clue.text: Find fee for change of address in Turkey

indicators.note: the letters of find fee are changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone works out a fee for changing their home address in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is a form of address, a title, not a home's location.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish title of respect, like sir, for an educated man.

clue.text: It reminds me more than once not to worry

indicators.note: the word me appears twice in a row, said more than once

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: worrying something tosses it about, so the letters of not are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone keeps telling themself not to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' doubles ME to MEME; 'to worry' turns NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake or souvenir is an object kept to recall a person or event.

clue.text: Many like dear Italian make, up

parts.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, a lot
as means like
cara is Italian for dear

explanation.surface: Many prefer cosmetics of a beloved Italian brand.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'make-up' so that it reads as 'make up' is the definition, cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye cosmetic applied to darken lashes.

clue.text: Some are picked, others pricked

parts.note: heads of corn are picked at harvest, while a listening animal's hearing organs are pricked up

explanation.surface: Seems to describe fruit or locks, some picked and some pricked.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses share one word: grain heads (of corn or wheat) are picked; the organs of hearing are pricked up when someone listens intently.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of cereal plants are gathered, and organs of hearing are raised when alert.

clue.text: Tails of these amphibians about twelve inches

definitions.text: Tails of these amphibians about twelve inches

indicators.note: the two final letters go around the abbreviation for a measure of length
the ends of the two words these and amphibians supply their final letters

parts.note: twelve inches make a foot, abbreviated FT

explanation.surface: Notes how long the tails of some small newts are, about a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tails of' takes E and S from 'these amphibians'; 'about' puts them around FT. Read whole, the clue describes the creatures themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Young newts, small amphibians, are called by this old word, the whole clue describing them.

clue.text: Far from quietly competent to produce fiction

parts.note: the opposite of quietly is loudly, forte in music, abbreviated F
competent means able

explanation.surface: Someone loud but capable sets out to write a story.
explanation.walkthrough: In musical scores p means quietly (piano) and f means loudly (forte), the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral tale or invented story, often with animals, is a kind of made-up narrative.

clue.text: More like Mood Indigo

parts.note: Duke Ellington's jazz number 'Mood Indigo' is a melancholy song, and indigo is also a deep colour, so more sad and more like that colour

explanation.surface: Compares something to the Duke Ellington jazz standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Mood Indigo, a Duke Ellington standard, is both a sad mood and a deep colour; the comparative covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word for both sad and indigo-coloured.

clue.text: Tool useful for the summer, say

indicators.note: say signals that we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, and adding is what a summer does

explanation.surface: Suggests a gardening implement handy in summer weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who sums; 'say' is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking cutting implement with a blade set at right angles to its handle.

clue.text: Remarkable boy has vanished

parts.note: if something has gone, there is none of it left, so no
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Notes that an extraordinary young lad has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade reads 'no Ted', the boy having vanished; NO comes first though the clue puts boy first.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable or celebrated: something worthy of remark is well known.

clue.text: Not important in 'USA so cash down

definitions.meaning: American slang for worthless or good-for-nothing
paying cash means nothing goes on a credit tab

explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a worthless person; and paying cash means nothing is charged to a credit tab.

clue.text: Something wrong in the parish records ?

definitions.text: Something wrong in the parish records

parts.words: Something wrong in the parish records
parts.note: a parish register is kept by the vicar, so a mistake there is literally a churchman's slip, though the phrase means an office typing slip

explanation.surface: Asks about a mistake in a church's register of births, marriages and deaths.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means an office or typing mistake; here 'clerical' is read as belonging to the clergy, who keep parish records.
explanation.definitionFit: An office mistake in copying or record-keeping; literally a churchman's slip in the parish register.
